source: A Night Off design doc pp. 34-36 (Seasonal nights). One is always on (the real calendar picks it; the host can force any); it is held at one bar (or either). Players choose the bar with it, or the bar without it. A seasonal night never removes the base game: it adds one layer and changes the odds.

seasons.name: The Harbour Festival
seasons.what: Fireworks at midnight; stalls in the yard (a ring toss, a strongman bell, a fish-guessing jar); the crowd is Packed; every event's odds double.
seasons.signature: The fireworks: for 60 s every flirt is one step easier and every fight is invisible to the police.
seasons.headline: FIREWORKS OVER THE GULL; {who} WINS THE FISH JAR AND WON'T SAY HOW

seasons.name: The Storm
seasons.what: The ferry stops; the power fails at a random hour (candles, no jukebox, no slots); the yard or the roof is closed; everyone who's in is in until it passes.
seasons.signature: A lock-in by weather: the bartender tells the story of the Marguerite in the dark.
seasons.headline: STORM LOCKS IN THE HARBOUR; THE MARGUERITE'S STORY TOLD AGAIN BY CANDLELIGHT
marguerite: "The Marguerite went out on a night like this, forty years ago."
"Her captain sat on that stool. Still does, some nights."
"They say the lamp in her wheelhouse was still lit when she went under."
"Twelve men. One came back. He never paid his tab again; we never asked."

seasons.name: The Wedding
seasons.what: Lord Ashby's daughter marries a sailor (the groom is Cutter Jones); the card room is the reception; a free bar for an hour; a toast mini-game.
seasons.signature: Objecting at the ceremony is a story.
seasons.headline: SOCIETY WEDDING AT THE BRASS MONKEY; {who} OBJECTS; THE GROOM 'NOT SURPRISED'
toasts: To the bride, who could do better, and the groom, who knows it!
To Lord Ashby, who lost his house twice and found a son-in-law once!
To the sea, which brought them together, and to the bar, which kept them there!
To love! And to the open bar, which is the same thing tonight!
I've known Cutter Jones for ten years and I still don't know his first name. To... him!

seasons.name: The Regatta
seasons.what: Rival crews from three ports; the darts and pool ladder pays triple; the midnight brawl is a tournament with a referee (Sister Ash).
seasons.signature: Winning the ladder sober is a headline that persists on the profile.
seasons.headline: REGATTA NIGHT AT THE GULL; {who} TAKES THE LADDER STONE-COLD SOBER

seasons.name: New Year
seasons.what: The clock runs to 4; a countdown at midnight; everyone kisses someone (a flirt roll for the whole room at once); the fortune teller reads the year.
seasons.signature: A player with no one to kiss kisses the goat.
seasons.headline: NEW YEAR AT THE HARBOUR; {who} RINGS IT IN WITH THE GOAT

seasons.name: The Wake of the Year
seasons.what: Deacon Pale's wake, bigger: the whole dock mourns; no fights are possible; a confession round at the bar where every patron tells one secret.
seasons.signature: Every kidney thief is named, once, by someone, if you listen.
seasons.headline: THE WHOLE DOCK MOURNS AT THE GULL; EVERY SECRET TOLD, NOT ONE PUNCH THROWN

seasons.name: The Masquerade
seasons.what: Masks for everyone: patrons' names and traits are hidden; tells still work; the kidney thieves are three instead of one.
seasons.signature: Unmasking a thief before midnight earns their cooler (it stops the next theft).
seasons.headline: MASKED BALL AT THE MONKEY; {who} UNMASKS A KIDNEY THIEF BEFORE MIDNIGHT

seasons.name: The Cook's Birthday
seasons.what: Tam cooks for free all night (sobering is free); the cook is Delighted and will fight anyone who doesn't eat.
seasons.signature: The only night the frying pan is given, not sold.
seasons.headline: THE COOK TURNS FIFTY; {who} LEAVES WITH HIS FRYING PAN, AS A GIFT
